linkedin.title: We are tired of news that is designed to make us angry.
linkedin.body:
Most news apps are built on a simple, flawed premise: the more time you spend scrolling, the better the product is working. This usually means prioritizing sensational headlines and constant alerts that spike your cortisol. It is a race to the bottom that leaves us feeling exhausted rather than informed.

At Headlinne, we are taking a different approach. We believe AI should be used to filter out the noise, not amplify it. Our goal is to respect your time by cutting straight to the substance of the stories that actually matter to you. You do not need twenty notifications a day to understand what is happening in the world. You just need a clear, concise summary of the events that shape your day.

Building a calmer news experience means focusing on clarity over volume. It means giving you control over what you see, so your feed reflects your interests instead of an algorithm's need for engagement. Smart news should feel like a relief, not a chore.
linkedin.cta: If you want to see how we are rethinking the daily news habit, you can take a look at HEADLINNE.com.

story_card.headline: Vijay Pande shifts from big VC to AI-focused biotech
story_card.standfirst: A top investor is changing his strategy for funding the future of medicine.

steps.label: What happened
steps.text: Vijay Pande left his $4 billion biotech role at a16z to launch VZVC. He is now making smaller bets.

steps.label: How we got here
steps.text: He spent years managing huge funds. Now he wants to focus on AI-native startups in the biology space.

steps.label: Why it matters
steps.text: Biology is moving from discovery to engineering. Yet, clinical trials remain incredibly expensive.

steps.label: What to watch
steps.text: Look for how he uses open, shared datasets to solve the high cost of drug development.

story_card.caption:
Vijay Pande is pivoting from his $4 billion fund at a16z to start a new AI-focused firm called VZVC.

Pande believes biology is finally becoming an engineering discipline rather than just a discovery science. He is betting that using AI and shared data will help solve the massive costs that still plague clinical trials today. It is a major shift from the high-volume investing style he used previously.
